title: Durably defer a procedure until a scheduled continuation
description:
As a procedure author, I want to durably defer a procedure until a host-scheduled time, so that transient external conditions release the worker and resume without being mistaken for completion.

Feature: Durable scheduled continuation
Scenario: A procedure defers without blocking a worker
  Given a running procedure requests a stable continuation key and a future resume time
  When Procedure.defer is called
  Then Tactus checkpoints the normalized request
  And exits with WAITING_FOR_TIME rather than success
  And does not sleep the worker thread

Scenario: Replay before the due time remains deferred
  Given a checkpointed scheduled continuation is not yet due
  When the procedure replays
  Then the same request remains authoritative
  And Tactus returns WAITING_FOR_TIME again

Scenario: Replay after the due time continues exactly once
  Given a checkpointed scheduled continuation is due
  When the host resumes the procedure
  Then Procedure.defer returns a completed continuation result
  And later replay does not create a second continuation boundary

Scenario: A changed request fails closed
  Given a scheduled continuation is already checkpointed
  When replay supplies a conflicting key or time
  Then Tactus rejects the conflict rather than silently replacing durable state

The primitive is host-neutral. Host persistence, scheduling, authorization, and product status mapping are out of scope.
